newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila says elections in April 1999.
newsitem.headline: Kabila says elections in April 1999.

text.p: President Laurent Kabila said on Thursday that the Democratic Republic of Congo would hold presidential and parliamentary elections in April 1999.
Kabila was speaking after his inauguration as head of state.
"We are not in a hurry. This crumbling and shattered state must be organised so that the Congolese people can hold elections," he said in an address to the nation from Kinshasa's main sports stadium.
"Be assured that the timetable will be respected," he said.
In a side-swipe at repeated Western calls for him to introduce democracy as quickly as possible, he added that no foreign interference would change the timetable.
Kabila's forces marched into Kinshasa on May 17 after seven months of civil war to end over three decades of rule by veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko, who fled into exile.
